name: schedule-quality-audit
title: Schedule quality audit
description: DCMA 14 quality audit of a P6 project: score and weighted grade, checks against their thresholds, engine check, trend since the previous audit, dangling ends, redundant links and float profile, with fixes proposed only. Use when the user asks to audit, check or score the quality of a schedule.

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID as shown in P6

template:
Schedule quality audit of project {project}: DCMA 14 checks, score and weighted grade, engine check, trend since the previous audit, dangling ends, redundant links and float profile. Fixes are proposed, never applied: this skill calls no write tool.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Each call is one page: the report shows that page and says when there are more,
so do not read further pages.
1. cv = p6_cpm_validate(project="{project}", limit=5): engine against the last F9: the critical path test relies on it.
2. hc = p6_health_check(project="{project}"): full DCMA 14 run: checks, score, thresholds, baseline (saves a snapshot).
3. tr = p6_health_check_compare(project="{project}", before="previous", after="latest"): trend since the previous audit (fails when there is none). If this call returns an error, keep its message as tr.error (its other fields are null).
4. dg = p6_dangling(project="{project}", limit=15): open starts and open finishes with a suggested link.
5. rd = p6_redundant_links(project="{project}", limit=15): links that are candidates for removal.
6. fa = p6_float_analysis(project="{project}"): total and free float distribution of the open activities.
7. fo_neg = p6_float_origin(project="{project}", task_code=<hc.checks.negative_float.worst.task_code>, limit=1): where the lowest negative float comes from. <hc.checks.negative_float.worst.task_code> is the field checks.negative_float.worst.task_code of the result of hc: when it is null or missing, skip this call (its fields are null).
8. fo_high = p6_float_origin(project="{project}", task_code=<hc.checks.high_float.worst.task_code>, limit=1): where the highest float comes from. <hc.checks.high_float.worst.task_code> is the field checks.high_float.worst.task_code of the result of hc: when it is null or missing, skip this call (its fields are null).

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

For this skill: the DCMA and trend tables have one row per key of hc.checks and tr.checks, the key in the
Check column, in the order returned; the weighted table one row per key of hc.weighted_score.checks. The dangling count adds open starts and open finishes: an activity
with both counts twice.

Fixes: the report only proposes them. Do not call a write tool in this skill. If the user then asks to
apply one, use the matching tool as a dry run first (p6_add_relationships with the items of a dangling
suggestion, p6_delete_relationships with the task_pred_id of a redundant link from rd), show its plan,
and apply it only after the user's explicit yes to that plan. Then ask the user to open P6, press F9
and run this audit again.

files.text:
# Schedule quality audit of {project}

Data date {data_date}, last schedule run (F9) {last_f9}. Every figure comes from the last F9 in P6; this audit changed nothing in the database.

[if: stale]
Warning: this project was changed after its last F9. Dates, float and the checks below are out of date until it is rescheduled in P6 (F9).
[end if]

[if not: trusted]
Warning: this server's CPM engine does not reproduce the last F9 of this project (match rate {match_rate}). The critical path test relies on it: its result is not reliable until the differences are explained (the logic-date-integrity skill lists them).
[end if]

## Score

- Checks passed: {score_passed} of {score_evaluated} evaluated ({score_pct}); failed: {score_failed}; not evaluated: {score_not_evaluated}.
- Weighted score: {w_points} points out of 100, grade {w_grade}. Engine match rate with the last F9: {match_rate}.
- Thresholds: {threshold_source}. Baseline of missed tasks and BEI: {baseline}.
- Open activities: {open_activities} (not completed, LOE and WBS summary left out).

[if not: baseline]
No baseline: missed tasks and BEI are not evaluated. Set a project baseline in P6 to evaluate them.
[end if]

Weighted score: each check below earns its weight when it passes, half when it fails within its warn band (an at most check up to twice its threshold, an at least check down to 0.9 times it; no band at a zero threshold) and nothing when it fails; a check not evaluated is left out, and the points are the earned weight out of the weight of the evaluated checks. Grades: A from 90 points, B from 80, C from 70, D from 55, F below.

[table: weighted]

## DCMA checks

Count and Out of: open activities (logic, hard_constraints, high_float, negative_float), open TT_Task and TT_Rsrc activities (high_duration, resources), links whose successor is open (leads, lags, long_lags, fs_links), all activities (invalid_dates), baseline activities due by the data date (missed_tasks; bei counts the completed activities out of them), constraint dates plus the must finish date (key_dates). LOE and WBS summary activities are always left out. Pass: % at most the threshold, except fs_links (at least); logic_density, cpli and bei compare their Value (at least the threshold). logic_density is links whose successor is open per open activity; it counts in the weighted score only, not in the checks passed above. key_dates is information only.

[table: dcma]

[if: cpt_activity]
Critical path test: {cpt_activity}, the earliest most critical open task, is delayed in this server's CPM engine; the test passes when the project finish moves about as much as that activity's own finish.
[end if]

## Trend since the previous audit

[if: trend_error]
No trend: there is no earlier audit of this project in this database. This run saved a snapshot; the next audit is compared with it.
[end if]

[table: trend]

## Dangling ends

Dangling ends: {dangling}, open starts (driven only by FF or SF predecessors) plus open finishes (driving only SS or SF successors); an activity with both counts twice.

[table: dangling]

## Redundant links

{redundant} links are candidates for removal. Removing all of them would leave {red_side_effects} open activities without a predecessor or a successor.

[table: redundant]

## Float profile

Total float of the open activities from {tf_min} d to {tf_max} d; negative: {tf_negative}; critical: {critical} ({critical_definition}).

[table: float]

## Proposed fixes

Proposals only: nothing was changed. A fix is applied by the user in P6, or through a dry run that the user reads and confirms; then the project is rescheduled (F9) and audited again.

[if: tf_negative]
- Negative float: {tf_negative} open activities, down to {tf_min} d. Recover the driving path (logic, durations, resources) or review the date it is measured against. Never delete a constraint only to clear negative float.
[end if]
[if: neg_expl]
  {neg_expl}
[end if]
[if: missed]
- Missed tasks: {missed} activities due by the baseline finished late or not at all. Re-plan their remaining work and its logic.
[end if]
[if: high_float]
- High float: {high_float} open activities above the limit. Check their successors: a missing link gives float that is not real.
[end if]
[if: high_expl]
  {high_expl}
[end if]
[if: logic_count]
- Open ends: {logic_count} open activities without a predecessor or a successor. Tie an open end to the work it really drives, never straight to the project finish.
[end if]
[if: lags]
- Lags: {lags} links with a positive lag. Replace a lag that stands for work (delivery, curing, review) by an activity.
[end if]
[if: dangling]
- Dangling ends: {dangling}. Add the suggested link after checking it, or an FS link if the work cannot overlap.
[end if]
[if not: fs_pass]
- Relationship types: do not convert SS or FF ties to FS only to pass fs_links: a link type follows how the work overlaps.
[end if]
[if: redundant]
- Redundant links: {redundant} candidates. Remove only a link that does not drive (Drives no), and check the activities it would leave without logic.
[end if]

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- A call says the project is not found: "Project <project> was not found: check the Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- p6_health_check says the project is an EPS node or has no data date: repeat its message and stop.

## Warnings (fixed wording in report.md)

- schedule_state.stale is true: keep the warning block, first in the report.
- hc.baseline is null: keep the "No baseline" block; missed_tasks and bei show "not evaluated".
- tr failed: keep the "No trend" block and leave the trend table out. A tr.error saying the project "has 1
  health snapshot(s)" (or 0) is the no-previous-audit case: the snapshot this audit just saved is the only
  one, and the block says all there is to say. Any other tr.error: repeat it after that block. Never work out
  a trend yourself.
- A check whose pass is null is written "not evaluated", never pass or fail.
- cv.trusted is false: keep the warning that the engine does not reproduce the last F9 (the critical path test
  relies on it).
- fo_neg and fo_high run only when hc gives a worst activity (negative or high float); a skipped one leaves its
  explanation out. Each explanation is copied as returned, under its fix.

## Cross-checks (each group must be equal)

1. cv, hc, dg, rd and fa schedule_state.data_date (same data date).
2. hc.open_incomplete_activities = fa.scope.activities.
3. hc.checks.negative_float.count = fa.stats.negative_tf.
4. hc.checks.logic.dangling.open_start.count = dg.counts.start.
5. hc.checks.logic.dangling.open_finish.count = dg.counts.finish.

If a group differs, the database changed between the calls: run the calls again once (the health check
saves one more snapshot). If it still differs, say which group differs and do not publish the figures it
concerns.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- The DCMA table has one row per key of hc.checks, in the order returned (logic_density included), with
  "none" for a missing threshold and "not evaluated" for a null pass. The weighted table has one row per key of
  hc.weighted_score.checks; the points and the grade are copied, never worked out from the rows.
- The paged tables (dangling 15, redundant 15) stop at their cap; when the call has more pages
  (next_offset not null) the table ends with "Showing the first <returned> of <total> ...", both numbers
  copied from that call.
- Activities are written "Activity ID - name", the link ends of the redundant links table too; its
  Categories cell lists every category of the link, joined by a comma.
- No write tool was called. Fixes are proposals; a fix is applied only through a dry run the user
  confirms explicitly, then F9 in P6.
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names and number formats exactly as
  formatted.

# Fields of Schedule quality audit

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. cv = p6_cpm_validate(project="{project}", limit=5): engine against the last F9: the critical path test relies on it.
2. hc = p6_health_check(project="{project}"): full DCMA 14 run: checks, score, thresholds, baseline (saves a snapshot).
3. tr = p6_health_check_compare(project="{project}", before="previous", after="latest"): trend since the previous audit (fails when there is none). If this call returns an error, keep its message as tr.error (its other fields are null).
4. dg = p6_dangling(project="{project}", limit=15): open starts and open finishes with a suggested link.
5. rd = p6_redundant_links(project="{project}", limit=15): links that are candidates for removal.
6. fa = p6_float_analysis(project="{project}"): total and free float distribution of the open activities.
7. fo_neg = p6_float_origin(project="{project}", task_code=<hc.checks.negative_float.worst.task_code>, limit=1): where the lowest negative float comes from. <hc.checks.negative_float.worst.task_code> is the field checks.negative_float.worst.task_code of the result of hc: when it is null or missing, skip this call (its fields are null).
8. fo_high = p6_float_origin(project="{project}", task_code=<hc.checks.high_float.worst.task_code>, limit=1): where the highest float comes from. <hc.checks.high_float.worst.task_code> is the field checks.high_float.worst.task_code of the result of hc: when it is null or missing, skip this call (its fields are null).

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.
